metadata.title: Bott Periodicity for Fibred Cusp Operators
metadata.source_note: Extracted from PDF->text fallback; .tex source not available. Math fidelity reduced.
metadata.registry_mismatch_note: metadata.json registry lists this as 'Regularity Lemma for k-Uniform Hypergraphs' by Rodl/Skokan, but the actual PDF (arxiv math/0408225) is 'Bott Periodicity for Fibred Cusp Operators' by Frederic Rochon. Title/authors taken from the PDF first page.

nodes.name: Fibred cusp vector field
nodes.statement: A fibred cusp vector field $V \in C^\infty(X, TX)$ is a vector field which, at the boundary $\partial X$, is tangent to the fibres of the fibration $\Phi$, and such that $Vx \in x^2 C^\infty(X)$, where $x$ is the defining function. Denote by $\mathcal{V}_\Phi(X)$the Lie algebra of fibred cusp vector fields.
nodes.statement_clean: A vector field tangent to fibres of Phi at the boundary, with normal component vanishing to order x^2.

nodes.name: Fibred cusp differential operators
nodes.statement: The space of fibred cusp differential operators of order $m$, $\mathrm{Diff}_\Phi^m(X)$, is the space of operators on $C^\infty(X)$ generated by $C^\infty(X)$ and products of up to $m$ elements of $\mathcal{V}_\Phi(X)$.

nodes.name: Fibred cusp density bundle
nodes.statement: The fibred cusp density bundle ${}^\Phi\Omega$ is the space of densities on $X$ locally of the form $\frac{\alpha}{x^{l+2}} dx\, dy\, dz$ near $\partial X$, with $l = \dim Y$. The right fibred cusp density bundle is ${}^\Phi\Omega'_R = \beta_\Phi^* \beta_b^* ({}^\Phi\Omega_R)$ on $X_\Phi^2$.

nodes.name: Phi-pseudodifferential operators
nodes.statement: For $m \in \mathbb{R}$, $\Psi_\Phi^m(X) = \{ K \in I^m(X_\Phi^2, \Delta_\Phi; {}^\Phi\Omega'_R) \mid K \equiv 0 \text{ at } \partial X_\Phi^2 \setminus \mathrm{ff}_\Phi\}$, with $I^m$ denoting conormal distributions of order $m$.

nodes.name: Fibred cusp tangent bundle
nodes.statement: The fibred cusp tangent bundle ${}^\Phi TX$ is the smooth vector bundle on $X$ such that $\mathcal{V}_\Phi(X) = C^\infty(X; {}^\Phi TX)$. Although ${}^\Phi TX \cong TX$, the isomorphism is not natural.

nodes.name: Symbol and elliptic Phi-operator
nodes.statement: If $P \in \Psi_\Phi^m(X; E, F)$, $\sigma_m(P)$ is the symbol of $P$. If $\sigma_m(P)$ is invertible, $P$ is elliptic.

nodes.name: Fully elliptic operator
nodes.statement: An operator $P \in \Psi_\Phi^m(X; E, F)$ is fully elliptic if it is elliptic and if its normal operator $N_\Phi(P)$ is invertible.

nodes.name: Weighted Sobolev spaces
nodes.statement: For $l, m \in \mathbb{R}$ with $m \ge 0$: $x^l H_\Phi^m(X; E) = \{u \in x^l L^2(X;E) \mid Pu \in x^l L^2(X;E)\ \forall P \in \Psi_\Phi^m(X;E)\}$ and dual definition for negative orders.
nodes.statement_clean: Weighted Sobolev spaces adapted to fibred cusp pseudodifferential operators.

nodes.name: Residue trace
nodes.statement: For $A \in \Psi_\Phi^{-\infty}(X; E)$, the residue trace $\mathrm{Tr}_R(A)$ is the residue at $z = 0$ of the meromorphic function $z \mapsto \mathrm{Tr}(x^z A)$.

nodes.name: Regularized trace
nodes.statement: The regularized trace $\overline{\mathrm{Tr}}(A)$ of $A \in \Psi_\Phi^{-\infty}(X;E)$ is $\overline{\mathrm{Tr}}(A) = \lim_{z \to 0}\bigl(\mathrm{Tr}(x^z A) - \frac{\mathrm{Tr}_R(A)}{z}\bigr)$.

nodes.name: Formal power series of suspended operators
nodes.statement: $\Psi_{\Phi s}^{-\infty}(\partial X; E)[[x]]$ denotes the space of formal power series in $x$ with coefficients in $\Psi_{\Phi s}^{-\infty}(\partial X; E)$.

nodes.name: Star-product
nodes.statement: For $a, b \in \Psi_{\Phi s}^{-\infty}(\partial X; E)[[x]]$, $a * b = \widehat{N'_\Phi(A \circ B)}$ where $A, B$ are chosen with $\widehat{N'_\Phi}(A) = a$ and $\widehat{N'_\Phi}(B) = b$. Independent of the choices.

nodes.name: Spectral section
nodes.statement: A spectral section $(\Pi_{M/B}, R_1, R_2)$ for the family of Laplacians $\Delta_{M/B}$ is a smooth family of projections with range a trivial vector bundle, plus reals $R_1 < R_2$, such that for all $b \in B$ and all eigenvalues $\lambda$: $\Pi_b s = s$ if $\lambda < R_1$ and $\Pi_b s = 0$ if $\lambda > R_2$.

nodes.name: Section asymptotic to the identity
nodes.statement: A smooth section of $\pi^* G^{-\infty}$ (or any bundle with a section $\mathrm{Id}$) is asymptotic to the identity if it converges rapidly with all derivatives to $\mathrm{Id}$ as one approaches infinity in $V$. Denote $\Gamma_{\mathrm{Id}}(V; \pi^* G^{-\infty})$.

nodes.name: Homotopy classes [V; GL(infinity, C)]
nodes.statement: $[V; GL(\infty, \mathbb{C})]$ denotes the homotopy classes of continuous maps $V \to GL(\infty, \mathbb{C})$ which converge to the identity at infinity in $V$.

nodes.name: Stabilized homotopy class [Id+S]_infty
nodes.statement: If $(\mathrm{Id}+S)$ is a section of $\pi^* G^{-\infty}$ asymptotic to the identity and $(\Pi, R_1, R_2)$ a compatible spectral section, $[\mathrm{Id}+S]_\infty$ is the homotopy class in $[V; GL(\infty, \mathbb{C})]$ of $\mathrm{Id}+\Pi S \Pi$ trivialized via the range of $\Pi$.

nodes.name: Homotopy classes [V; pi^*G^-infty]
nodes.statement: $[V; \pi^* G^{-\infty}]$ denotes the set of homotopy classes of smooth sections of $\pi^* G^{-\infty}$ asymptotic to the identity.

nodes.name: Direct sum bundle E (dim Z = 0 case)
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{E} \to Y$ be the complex vector bundle with fibre at $y \in Y$ given by $\mathcal{E}_y = \bigoplus_{z \in \Phi^{-1}(y)} E_z$.

nodes.name: GL(E,C) and pull-back
nodes.statement: $GL(\mathcal{E}, \mathbb{C})$ is the bundle over $Y$ with fibre $GL(\mathcal{E}_y, \mathbb{C})$. $\pi^* GL(\mathcal{E}, \mathbb{C}) \to {}^\Phi N^* Y$ is the pull-back.

nodes.name: Homotopy class via inclusion (dim Z = 0)
nodes.statement: If $(\mathrm{Id}+S)$ is the indicial family of an operator in $\mathcal{F}_\Phi^{-\infty}(X;E)$ and $\mathcal{E}\oplus\mathcal{F}\cong\mathbb{C}^n$, then $[\mathrm{Id}+S]_\infty \in [{}^\Phi N^* Y; GL(\infty;\mathbb{C})]$ is the homotopy class of the associated map $\mathrm{Id}+S_F: {}^\Phi N^* Y \to GL(\infty;\mathbb{C})$.

nodes.name: Associated K-class kappa(Id+A)
nodes.statement: If $(\mathrm{Id}+\widehat{A}_0)$ is the indicial family of $(\mathrm{Id}+A)\in\mathcal{F}_\Phi^{-\infty}(X;E)$, then $\kappa(\mathrm{Id}+A)\in K_c^0(T^*Y)$ is the K-class associated to $[\mathrm{Id}+\widehat{A}_0]_\infty$ via $[{}^\Phi N^* Y; GL(\infty,\mathbb{C})] \cong K_c^0(T^*Y)$.

nodes.name: Inclusion i_1 in K-theory of boundary
nodes.statement: $i_1: K_c^0(T^*Y) \hookrightarrow K_c^0(T^*\partial W_Y) \cong K_c^0(T^*Y_0)\oplus K_c^0(T^*Y_1)$, $a \mapsto (0, a)$, where $W_Y = [0,1]_t \times Y$.

nodes.name: Clutching K-class c(Id+S)
nodes.statement: For $(\mathrm{Id}+S) \in \mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{Id}}^{-\infty}(W_Y; \mathbb{C}^n)$, $c(\mathrm{Id}+S) \in K_c^0(T^*V_Y)$ is the element defined by applying the clutching construction to the indicial family $\mathrm{Id}+\widehat{S}_0: {}^{\mathrm{Id}}N^*\partial W_Y \to GL(n,\mathbb{C})$.

nodes.name: Group of invertible smoothing perturbations G^-infty_Phi
nodes.statement: $G_\Phi^{-\infty}(X;E) \subset \mathcal{F}_\Phi^{-\infty}(X;E)$ is the group of invertible operators $\{\mathrm{Id}+A \mid A \in \Psi_\Phi^{-\infty}(X;E),\ (\mathrm{Id}+A) \text{ invertible}\}$.

nodes.name: Subgroup vanishing at boundary Gdot^-infty
nodes.statement: $\dot{G}^{-\infty}(X;E) = \{\mathrm{Id}+Q \mid Q \in x^\infty \Psi_\Phi^{-\infty}(X;E),\ \mathrm{Id}+Q \text{ invertible}\}$.

nodes.name: Suspended invertibles G^-infty_Phi s
nodes.statement: $G_{\Phi s}^{-\infty}(\partial X; E) = \{\mathrm{Id}+Q \mid Q \in \Psi_{\Phi s}^{-\infty}(\partial X; E),\ \mathrm{Id}+Q \text{ invertible}\}$. Identified with $\Gamma_{\mathrm{Id}}({}^\Phi N^* Y; \pi^* G^{-\infty})$ via Fourier transform.

nodes.name: Index-zero subspaces F_Phi,0 and G_Phi s,0
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{F}_{\Phi,0}^{-\infty}(X;E)$ denotes Fredholm operators of index zero in $\mathcal{F}_\Phi^{-\infty}(X;E)$; $G_{\Phi s,0}^{-\infty}(\partial X;E) = N_\Phi(\widehat{\mathcal{F}_{\Phi,0}^{-\infty}(X;E)})$ and $G_{\Phi s,0}^{-\infty}(X;E)[[x]] = N'_\Phi(\widehat{\mathcal{F}_{\Phi,0}^{-\infty}(X;E)})$ with composition by the $*$-product.

nodes.name: Pointed homotopy classes [M; F_Phi^-infty]
nodes.statement: For a compact pointed manifold $(M, m_0)$, $[M; \mathcal{F}_\Phi^{-\infty}(X;E)]$ is the set of homotopy classes of continuous maps $M \to \mathcal{F}_\Phi^{-\infty}(X;E)$ sending $m_0$ to the identity.

nodes.name: Generalized index map ind: [M; F_Phi^-infty] -> K^0(M)
nodes.statement: For $T: M \to \mathcal{F}_\Phi^{-\infty}(X;E)$ with $T_{m_0}=\mathrm{Id}$ and $V \subset H$ closed of finite codimension with $V \cap \ker T_m = \{0\}$, $\mathrm{ind}(T) = [H/V] - [H/T(V)] \in \widetilde{K}^0(M)$.

nodes.name: Weak deformation retract
nodes.statement: $U \subset T$ is a weak deformation retract of $T$ if for any closed manifold $M$ and any continuous map $f: M \to T$, there is a continuous $g$ homotopic to $f$ with $g(M) \subset U$.

nodes.name: Small open ball in G^-infty_Phi
nodes.statement: An open ball $B_\epsilon(A) = \{\mathrm{Id}+Q \mid Q \in \Psi_\Phi^{-\infty}(X;E),\ \|A-\mathrm{Id}-Q\| < \epsilon\}$ centered at $A \in G_\Phi^{-\infty}(X;E)$ is small if $B_{3\epsilon}(A) \subset G_\Phi^{-\infty}(X;E)$.

nodes.name: Local form of Phi-pseudodifferential operator action
nodes.statement: For $\chi \in C^\infty(X)$ supported in $(U,(x,y,z))$ meeting $\partial X$, the action of $P \in \Psi_\Phi^m(X)$ on $u \in C_c^\infty(U)$ is $(\chi P u)(x,y,z) = \int P_\chi(x,y,z,S,Y,z-z')\tilde u(x(1-xS), y - xY, z')\, dS\, dY\, dz'$ with $S=(x-x')/x^2$, $Y=(y-y')/x$.
assumptions: $\chi \in C^\infty(X)$ has support in coordinate patch $(U,(x,y,z))$ with $U \cap \partial X \ne \emptyset$
conclusions: $(\chi P u)(x,y,z) = \int P_\chi(x,y,z,S,Y,z-z')\tilde u(x(1-xS), y - xY, z')\, dS\, dY\, dz'$ with $P_\chi$ conormal to $\{S=Y=0\}\times\{z=z'\}$ and rapidly decreasing as $|(S,Y)|\to\infty$.

nodes.name: Composition of Phi-operators
nodes.statement: $\Psi_\Phi^m(X; F, G) \circ \Psi_\Phi^n(X; E, F) \subset \Psi_\Phi^{m+n}(X; E, G)$.
conclusions: $\Psi_\Phi^m(X; F, G) \circ \Psi_\Phi^n(X; E, F) \subset \Psi_\Phi^{m+n}(X; E, G)$

nodes.name: Symbol short exact sequence
nodes.statement: For all $m \in \mathbb{Z}$ there exists $\sigma_m: \Psi_\Phi^m(X;E,F) \to C^\infty({}^\Phi S^* X; \hom(E,F)\otimes R^m)$ giving a short exact sequence $\Psi_\Phi^{m-1} \hookrightarrow \Psi_\Phi^m \xrightarrow{\sigma_m} C^\infty(\dots)$.

nodes.name: Normal operator short exact sequence
nodes.statement: For any $m \in \mathbb{R}$, $x\Psi_\Phi^m(X;E,F) \hookrightarrow \Psi_\Phi^m(X;E,F) \xrightarrow{N_\Phi} \Psi_{\Phi s}^m(\partial X; E, F)$ is exact, with $N_\Phi$ multiplicative ($N_\Phi(AB) = N_\Phi(A)\circ N_\Phi(B)$). $N_\Phi$ is restriction of the Schwartz kernel to the front face $\mathrm{ff}_\Phi$.

nodes.name: Fredholm criterion (full ellipticity)
nodes.statement: $P \in \Psi_\Phi^m(X; E, F)$ is Fredholm as $P: x^l H_\Phi^{m'}(X;E)\to x^l H_\Phi^{m'-m}(X;F)$ for any $l, m'$ if and only if it is fully elliptic.

nodes.name: Elliptic regularity for fully elliptic operators
nodes.statement: The null space of a fully elliptic $P \in \Psi_\Phi^m(X;E,F)$ is contained in $\dot C^\infty(X;E)$, the smooth sections vanishing in Taylor series at $\partial X$.

nodes.name: Suspended operators as smooth sections
nodes.statement: There is a one-to-one correspondence between $\Psi_{\Phi s}^{-\infty}(\partial X;E,F)$ and smooth sections of $\pi^* P^{-\infty} \to {}^\Phi N^* Y$ rapidly decreasing with all derivatives at infinity in ${}^\Phi N^* Y \cong T^*Y\times\mathbb{R}$.

nodes.name: Trace-defect formula
nodes.statement: For $A, B \in \Psi_\Phi^{-\infty}(X;E)$, $\overline{\mathrm{Tr}}([A,B]) = \mathrm{Tr}_R((D_{\log x} A) B)$, where $D_{\log x} A = \partial_z A_z|_{z=0}$ and $A_z = x^{-z}[x^z, A]$.

nodes.name: Index formula via trace defect
nodes.statement: The index of $(\mathrm{Id}+A) \in \mathcal{F}_\Phi^{-\infty}(X;E)$ is $\mathrm{ind}(\mathrm{Id}+A) = \frac{1}{(2\pi)^{l+1}} \int_{{}^\Phi N^*Y} \mathrm{Tr}_{\Phi^{-1}(y)}\bigl(\widehat{(D_{\log x}AB)}_{l+1}(y,\tau,\eta)\bigr) dy\, d\eta\, d\tau$, where $(\mathrm{Id}+B)$ is a parametrix.
conclusions: Index given by integral of $(l+1)$-st Taylor coefficient of $\widehat{D_{\log x}AB}$ over ${}^\Phi N^*Y$

nodes.name: Index depends only on indicial-family homotopy class
nodes.statement: The index of $(\mathrm{Id}+A) \in \mathcal{F}_\Phi^{-\infty}(X;E)$ depends only on the homotopy class of the indicial family $\mathrm{Id}+\widehat A_0$ as an invertible asymptotic-to-identity section of $\pi^* P^{-\infty}$.

nodes.name: Star-product structure
nodes.statement: There exist differential operators $P_{k,j,l}, Q_{k,j,l}$ on sections of $P^{-\infty}$ such that for $a = \sum x^j a_j$, $b = \sum x^j b_j$, $a*b = \sum_{k\ge 1}\sum_{j+l\le k} x^k (P_{k,j,l} a_j)\circ(Q_{k,j,l} b_l)$. If $\Phi$ is trivial, $P_{k,j,l}, Q_{k,j,l}$ are independent of $Z$.

nodes.name: Existence of spectral section (Melrose)
nodes.statement: For a family of Laplacians $\Delta_{M/B}$ as in (4.1) and $R > 0$, there exists $R' > R$ and a smooth family of projections $\Pi_{M/B}$ such that $(\Pi_{M/B}, R, R')$ is a spectral section.
assumptions: $\Delta_{M/B}$ family of Laplacians on a fibration with closed fibres and compact base
conclusions: $\exists R' > R$ and a smooth family of projections $\Pi_{M/B}$ with range a trivial bundle, forming a spectral section $(\Pi_{M/B}, R, R')$

nodes.name: Well-definedness of [Id+S]_infty
nodes.statement: The homotopy class $[\mathrm{Id}+S]_\infty$ of definition 5.7 is independent of the trivialization of $F$, the spectral section, and the family of Laplacians.

nodes.name: I_infty is an isomorphism (dim Z > 0)
nodes.statement: The canonical map $I_\infty: [V; \pi^* G^{-\infty}] \to [V; GL(\infty, \mathbb{C})]$, $[\mathrm{Id}+S] \mapsto [\mathrm{Id}+S]_\infty$ is an isomorphism of sets.

nodes.name: Well-definedness of [Id+S]_infty (dim Z = 0)
nodes.statement: For $\dim Z = 0$, $[\mathrm{Id}+S]_\infty$ does not depend on the choice of complementary bundle $F$ with $\mathcal{E}\oplus\mathcal{F}$ trivial nor on the trivialization of $\mathcal{E}\oplus\mathcal{F}$.

nodes.name: Index of scattering operator via clutching
nodes.statement: For $(\mathrm{Id}+S) \in \mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{Id}}^{-\infty}(W_Y; \mathbb{C}^n)$, $\mathrm{ind}(\mathrm{Id}+S) = \mathrm{ind}_t(c(\mathrm{Id}+S))$, where $\mathrm{ind}_t: K_c^0(T^*V_Y)\to\mathbb{Z}$ is the topological index map.
nodes.origin_citation: Special case of theorem 6.4 in Melrose, Geometric scattering theory, 1995

nodes.name: Homotopy groups of F_Phi^-infty
nodes.statement: $\pi_k(\mathcal{F}_\Phi^{-\infty}(X;E)) \cong K_c^0(T^*Y)$ if $k$ even and $\widetilde K^{-1}(Y^{T^*Y})$ if $k$ odd.

nodes.name: Boundary homomorphism realizes the index map
nodes.statement: For $k \in \mathbb{N}$, the homomorphism $c \circ \partial \circ N_{\Phi *}: \pi_k(\mathcal{F}_\Phi^{-\infty}(X;E)) \to \widetilde K^0(S^k)$ equals the generalized index map of definition 7.13 with $M = S^k$.

nodes.name: Surjectivity of the boundary homomorphism
nodes.statement: For $k \in \mathbb{N}$, $\partial: \pi_k(G_{\Phi s,0}^{-\infty}(X;E)[[x]]) \to \pi_{k-1}(\dot G^{-\infty}(X;E))$ is surjective.

nodes.name: Weak contractibility implies contractibility of G^-infty_Phi
nodes.statement: If $G_\Phi^{-\infty}(X;E)$ is weakly contractible, then it is contractible. In particular, for the trivial fibration $\Phi: \partial X \to \mathrm{pt}$, $G_\Phi^{-\infty}(X;E)$ is contractible.

nodes.name: Meromorphic extension of Tr(x^z A)
nodes.statement: For $A \in \Psi_\Phi^{-\infty}(X;E)$, $\mathrm{Tr}(x^z A)$ is holomorphic for $\mathrm{Re}\{z\} > l+1$ and admits a meromorphic extension to $\mathbb{C}$ with at most simple poles at $l+1-\mathbb{N}_0$.
conclusions: Meromorphic extension to $\mathbb{C}$ with simple poles at $l+1-\mathbb{N}_0$

nodes.name: Surjectivity of full normal operator
nodes.statement: The full normal operator $N'_\Phi: \Psi_\Phi^{-\infty}(X;E) \to \Psi_{\Phi s}^{-\infty}(\partial X;E)[[x]]$ is surjective.

nodes.name: Indicial expansion of D_log x A
nodes.statement: If $\widehat{N'_\Phi(A)} = \widehat A_0$, then $\widehat{N'_\Phi(D_{\log x} A)} = \sum_{k\ge 1} \frac{x^k D_\tau^k \widehat A_0}{k}$.

nodes.name: Spectral approximation of asymptotic-to-identity sections
nodes.statement: For $(\mathrm{Id}+S)$ a smooth section of $\pi^* G^{-\infty}\to V$ asymptotic to the identity, there exists a spectral section $(\Pi, R_1, R_2)$ for $\Delta_{\partial X/Y}$ with $\|S_b - \Pi_b S_b \Pi_b\| < \frac{1}{2\|(\mathrm{Id}+S_b)^{-1}\|}$ for all $b\in V$.
assumptions: $(\mathrm{Id}+S)$ smooth section of $\pi^* G^{-\infty}\to V$ asymptotic to the identity
conclusions: $\exists$ spectral section $(\Pi, R_1, R_2)$ for $\Delta_{\partial X/Y}$ with $\|S_b - \Pi_b S_b \Pi_b\| < \frac{1}{2\|(\mathrm{Id}+S_b)^{-1}\|}$ for all $b\in V$

nodes.name: Independence from trivialization of F
nodes.statement: For $\Delta_{\partial X/Y}$ and $(\Pi, R_1, R_2)$ fixed, $[\mathrm{Id}+S]_\infty$ does not depend on the way $F$ is trivialized.

nodes.name: Independence from spectral section
nodes.statement: For fixed $\Delta_{\partial X/Y}$ and $(\mathrm{Id}+S)$ as in lemma 5.3, two spectral sections $(\Pi_1, R_1, T_1)$, $(\Pi_2, R_2, T_2)$ yield the same homotopy class $[\mathrm{Id}+S_{\Pi_i}]$ in $[V; GL(\infty, \mathbb{C})]$.

nodes.name: Independence from family of Laplacians
nodes.statement: $[\mathrm{Id}+S]_\infty$ does not depend on the choice of family of Laplacians $\Delta_{\partial X/Y}$.

nodes.name: [Id+S]_infty depends only on homotopy class
nodes.statement: If $(\mathrm{Id}+S)$ is a section of $\pi^* G^{-\infty}$ asymptotic to the identity, then $[\mathrm{Id}+S]_\infty \in [V; GL(\infty, \mathbb{C})]$ depends only on $[\mathrm{Id}+S] \in [V; \pi^* G^{-\infty}]$.

nodes.name: Index reduction to scattering operator (kernel)
nodes.statement: If $(\mathrm{Id}+A)\in\mathcal{F}_\Phi^{-\infty}(X;E)$ has indicial family $\widehat A_0$ lying in some subbundle $\pi^*\mathrm{End}(F)\subset\pi^*P^{-\infty}$ with $F\to Y$ trivial finite-rank, then any scattering operator $(\mathrm{Id}+S)\in\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{Id}}^{-\infty}(W_Y; F)$ with $\kappa(\mathrm{Id}+S) = i_1\kappa(\mathrm{Id}+A)$ has the same index as $\mathrm{Id}+A$.

nodes.name: Index-preserving reduction to a scattering operator
nodes.statement: For $(\mathrm{Id}+A)\in\mathcal{F}_\Phi^{-\infty}(X;E)$ and a sufficiently large trivial $F$, there exists a scattering operator $(\mathrm{Id}+S)\in\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{Id}}^{-\infty}(W_Y; F)$ with associated K-class $i_1\kappa(\mathrm{Id}+A)$ and $\mathrm{ind}(\mathrm{Id}+A) = \mathrm{ind}(\mathrm{Id}+S)$.

nodes.name: Homotopy groups of G_Phi s^-infty
nodes.statement: $\pi_k(G_{\Phi s}^{-\infty}(\partial X;E)) \cong K_c^0(T^*Y)$ for $k$ even and $\widetilde K^{-1}(Y^{T^*Y})$ for $k$ odd.

nodes.name: Serre fibration from full normal operator
nodes.statement: $\dot G^{-\infty}(X;E) \hookrightarrow G_\Phi^{-\infty}(X;E) \xrightarrow{N'_\Phi} G_{\Phi s,0}^{-\infty}(X;E)[[x]]$ is a short exact sequence and a Serre fibration.

nodes.name: Connected components of G^-infty_Phi
nodes.statement: $\pi_0(G_\Phi^{-\infty}(X;E)) \cong \ker\bigl(\mathrm{ind}_t: K_c^0(T^*Y) \to \mathbb{Z}\bigr)$.

nodes.name: Choice of V with smooth-vanishing complements
nodes.statement: The vector space $V$ in definition 7.13 may be chosen so that $V^\perp \subset \dot C^\infty(X;E)$ and $T_m(V)^\perp \subset \dot C^\infty(X;E)$ for all $m\in M$. If $\mathrm{ind}(T) = 0$, $V$ may be chosen so that $V^\perp$ and $T(V)^\perp$ are isomorphic.

nodes.name: Weak deformation retract under stabilization
nodes.statement: Under the inclusion $i': \mathcal{F}_\Phi^{-\infty}(X;E) \hookrightarrow \mathcal{F}_\Phi^{-\infty}(X;E^n)$ from $E\hookrightarrow E\otimes\mathbb{C}^n$, $\mathcal{F}_\Phi^{-\infty}(X;E)$ is a weak deformation retract of $\mathcal{F}_\Phi^{-\infty}(X;E^n)$.

nodes.name: Topological index formula for Fredholm fibred cusp operators
nodes.statement: The index of a Fredholm operator $(\mathrm{Id}+A) \in \mathcal{F}_\Phi^{-\infty}(X;E)$ is $\mathrm{ind}(\mathrm{Id}+A) = \mathrm{ind}_t(\kappa(\mathrm{Id}+A))$, where $\kappa(\mathrm{Id}+A) \in K_c^0(T^*Y)$ is the associated K-class and $\mathrm{ind}_t$ is the Atiyah-Singer topological index map.

nodes.name: Bott periodicity for fibred cusp operators
nodes.statement: For $k \in \mathbb{N}_0$ and $\dim Z > 0$, $\pi_{2k+1}(G_\Phi^{-\infty}(X;E)) \cong \widetilde K^{-1}(Y^{T^*Y})$ and $\pi_{2k}(G_\Phi^{-\infty}(X;E)) \cong \ker(\mathrm{ind}_t: K_c^0(T^*Y)\to\mathbb{Z})$.

nodes.name: Indicial family of Fredholm op as section of pi*G^-infty
nodes.statement: For $V = {}^\Phi N^* Y$, the indicial family $\mathrm{Id}+\widehat A_0$ of a Fredholm operator in $\mathcal{F}_\Phi^{-\infty}(X;E)$ corresponds to a section of $\pi^* G^{-\infty} \to {}^\Phi N^*Y$ asymptotic to the identity.

nodes.name: Homotopy of Id+S and Id+Pi S Pi
nodes.statement: Let $(\Pi, R_1, R_2)$ be the spectral section of lemma 5.3. Then $\mathrm{Id}+S$ and $\mathrm{Id}+\Pi S\Pi$ are homotopic as sections of $\pi^* G^{-\infty}$ asymptotic to the identity.

nodes.name: Indicial family as section of pi^*GL(E,C) (dim Z = 0)
nodes.statement: When $\dim Z = 0$, the indicial family $(\mathrm{Id}+\widehat A_0)$ of a Fredholm operator in $\mathcal{F}_\Phi^{-\infty}(X;E)$ is a section of $\pi^* GL(\mathcal{E}; \mathbb{C})$ asymptotic to the identity.

nodes.name: Surjectivity of index when dim Z > 0
nodes.statement: When $\dim Z > 0$, the index map $\mathrm{ind}: \mathcal{F}_\Phi^{-\infty}(X;E) \to \mathbb{Z}$ is surjective.

nodes.name: Surjectivity of index when dim Z = 0 (after stabilization)
nodes.statement: When $\dim Z = 0$, the index map $\mathrm{ind}: \mathcal{F}_\Phi^{-\infty}(X;\mathbb{C}^n) \to \mathbb{Z}$ is surjective for $n \in \mathbb{N}$ large enough.

nodes.name: Long exact sequence of homotopy groups
nodes.statement: The Serre fibration of lemma 7.9 yields a long exact sequence $\cdots \xrightarrow{\partial} \pi_k(\dot G^{-\infty}) \to \pi_k(G_\Phi^{-\infty}) \to \pi_k(G_{\Phi s,0}^{-\infty}) \xrightarrow{\partial} \pi_{k-1}(\dot G^{-\infty}) \to \cdots$ down to $\pi_0$.

nodes.name: Weak contractibility of G^-infty_Phi for cusp operators
nodes.statement: If $\Phi: \partial X \to \{\mathrm{pt}\}$ is the trivial fibration (cusp operators), then $G_\Phi^{-\infty}(X;E)$ is weakly contractible: all its homotopy groups (including $\pi_0$) are trivial.
conclusions: All homotopy groups of $G_\Phi^{-\infty}(X;E)$ are trivial

nodes.name: Disconnected boundary case (B_Phi)
nodes.statement: When $\partial X$ is disconnected, the same definition of $B_\Phi$ and $\mathrm{ff}_b$ is used, differing from [11], to make the disconnected-case generalization straightforward.

nodes.name: Finite covering case for P^-infty bundle
nodes.statement: When $\dim Z = 0$ and $\Phi: \partial X \to Y$ is a finite covering, $P^{-\infty}$ is the homomorphism bundle $\hom(\mathcal{E},\mathcal{F})$ where $\mathcal{E}_y = \bigoplus_{z\in\Phi^{-1}(y)} E_z$.

nodes.name: Order-m suspended operators correspondence
nodes.statement: For $P \in \Psi_{\Phi s}^m(\partial X; E, F)$ with general $m$, sections of the appropriate bundle $\pi^* P^m$ at infinity must be allowed to grow at most homogeneously of order $m$, with controlled derivatives.

nodes.name: Trace class agrees with regularized trace
nodes.statement: For $A \in x^{l+2}\Psi_\Phi^{-\infty}(X;E)$, $A$ is of trace class and $\overline{\mathrm{Tr}}(A) = \mathrm{Tr}(A)$.

nodes.name: Triviality of range in spectral section definition
nodes.statement: The triviality of the range of the spectral section is added beyond the original definition because only spectral sections with trivial range will be considered. Discreteness of the spectrum forces this bundle to be of finite rank.

nodes.name: Smooth versus continuous homotopy classes
nodes.statement: Passing from smooth to continuous maps does not change the set of homotopy classes (cf. proposition 17.8 in [5]).

nodes.name: Identification of Gdot^-infty with G^-infty matrices
nodes.statement: $\dot G^{-\infty}(X;E)$ identifies with $G^{-\infty}$, the group of semi-infinite invertible matrices satisfying (5.4), via eigensections vanishing at the boundary; hence $\dot G^{-\infty}(X;E)$ is a classifying space for odd K-theory and is independent of the fibred cusp structure.

nodes.name: Connected components of G_Phi s,0^-infty equal kernel of ind_t
nodes.statement: $G_{\Phi s,0}^{-\infty}(\partial X;E)$ has the same homotopy groups as $G_{\Phi s}^{-\infty}(\partial X;E)$ but fewer components: $\pi_0(G_{\Phi s,0}^{-\infty}(\partial X;E)) \cong \ker(\mathrm{ind}_t: K_c^0(T^*Y)\to\mathbb{Z})$. The $x^0$-truncation gives a deformation retraction of $G_{\Phi s,0}^{-\infty}(X;E)[[x]]$ onto $G_{\Phi s,0}^{-\infty}(X;E)$.

nodes.name: Atiyah-Singer topological index
nodes.statement: The topological index map $\mathrm{ind}_t: K_c^0(T^*Y) \to \mathbb{Z}$ on a closed manifold $Y$ equals the analytic index for symbol classes coming from elliptic pseudodifferential operators.
nodes.origin_citation: Atiyah and Singer, 'The index of elliptic operators: I', Ann. of Math. 87 (1968), 484-530

nodes.name: Bott periodicity (classical)
nodes.statement: $\pi_k(GL(\infty, \mathbb{C})) = \{0\}$ for $k$ even and $\mathbb{Z}$ for $k$ odd; equivalently $\widetilde K^0 \cong \widetilde K^{-2}$.
nodes.origin_citation: Bott, 'The stable homotopy of the classical groups', Ann. of Math. 70 (1959), 313-337

nodes.name: Kuiper's theorem
nodes.statement: The general linear group $GL(H)$ of a separable infinite-dimensional Hilbert space $H$ is contractible in the operator-norm topology. Equivalently, the Hilbert bundle $L^2(M/B; E)$ is trivial.
nodes.origin_citation: Kuiper, 'The homotopy type of the unitary group of Hilbert space', Topology 3 (1964), 19-30

nodes.name: Proof of TP292.1 (topological index formula)
nodes.statement: By lemma 6.3, reduce to a scattering operator $(\mathrm{Id}+S)$ with $\kappa(\mathrm{Id}+S) = i_1\kappa(\mathrm{Id}+A)$; apply proposition 6.5 and the Thom-isomorphism / push-forward identification $c(\mathrm{Id}+S) = i_!\kappa(\mathrm{Id}+A)$, then use $\mathrm{ind}_t \circ i_! = \mathrm{ind}_t$.

nodes.name: Proof of TP292.2 (Bott periodicity)
nodes.statement: By the surjectivity of $\partial$ (proposition 7.18), split the long exact sequence (7.2) into short exact sequences for odd and even degrees and identify each term using lemma 7.5 / proposition 7.6 and remark 7.8. The even case uses the classification of finitely generated $\mathbb{Z}$-modules.

nodes.name: Decompose long exact sequence using surjectivity of $\partial$
nodes.statement: Surjectivity of $\partial$ (proposition 7.18) decomposes the long exact sequence (7.2) into short exact sequences $0 \to \pi_{2k-1}(G_\Phi^{-\infty}) \to \pi_{2k-1}(G_{\Phi s,0}^{-\infty}) \to 0$ and $0 \to \pi_{2k}(G_\Phi^{-\infty}) \to \pi_{2k}(G_{\Phi s,0}^{-\infty}) \xrightarrow{\partial} \pi_{2k-1}(\dot G^{-\infty}) \to 0$.

nodes.name: Conclude odd case from short exact sequence
nodes.statement: For odd homotopy groups, $\pi_{2k-1}(G_\Phi^{-\infty}) \cong \pi_{2k-1}(G_{\Phi s,0}^{-\infty}) \cong \widetilde K^{-1}(Y^{T^*Y})$ via remark 7.8 / lemma 7.5.

nodes.name: Even case via classification of f.g. Z-modules
nodes.statement: For even degrees, propositions 7.6 and 7.15 rewrite the short exact sequence as $0\to\pi_{2k}(G_\Phi^{-\infty})\to\pi_{2k}(\mathcal{F}_\Phi^{-\infty})\xrightarrow{\mathrm{ind}}\widetilde K^0(S^{2k})\to 0$. Since $\pi_{2k}(\mathcal{F}_\Phi^{-\infty})\cong K_c^0(T^*Y)$ is finitely generated and $\widetilde K^0(S^{2k})\cong\mathbb{Z}$, classification of f.g. $\mathbb{Z}$-modules makes $\ker$ unique up to isomorphism. Since $\mathrm{ind}_t$ is also surjective, the kernel is $\ker\,\mathrm{ind}_t$.

nodes.name: Proof of PrP292.20 (contractibility of G_Phi^-infty)
nodes.statement: Cover $G_\Phi^{-\infty}(X;E)$ by countably many small balls $B_{\epsilon_i}(A_i)$ with locally finite refinement and partition of unity $\{\phi_i\}$. The homotopy $\xi_t(z) = (1-t)z + t\sum\phi_i(z) A_i$ retracts the space to the nerve $N$ of the covering, which is a CW complex; the inclusion $N\hookrightarrow G_\Phi^{-\infty}$ is a homotopy equivalence; Whitehead's theorem then concludes contractibility.

nodes.name: Construct locally finite covering by small balls and partition of unity
nodes.statement: Cover $G_\Phi^{-\infty}(X;E)$ by small balls $\{B_{\epsilon_i}(A_i)\}_{i\in\mathbb{N}}$. Paracompactness in operator norm allows a locally finite refinement with partition of unity $\{\phi_i\}$, continuous in the $C^\infty$-topology.

nodes.name: Define homotopy and verify range
nodes.statement: Define $\xi_t(z) = (1-t)z + t\sum_{i\in\mathbb{N}}\phi_i(z) A_i$. The 'small ball' condition $B_{3\epsilon}(A)\subset G_\Phi^{-\infty}$ ensures $\xi_t(z) \in G_\Phi^{-\infty}(X;E)$ for all $t \in [0,1]$.

nodes.name: Apply Whitehead's theorem to the nerve
nodes.statement: Let $N$ be the nerve of the cover (a CW complex with affine simplices). The inclusion $\rho: N \to G_\Phi^{-\infty}(X;E)$ sending vertex $b_i\mapsto A_i$ is a homotopy equivalence by $\xi_1$. Whitehead's theorem then gives contractibility from weak contractibility.

nodes.name: Local form of fibred cusp vector field
nodes.statement: $V = ax^2\frac{\partial}{\partial x} + \sum_{i=1}^l b_i x \frac{\partial}{\partial y_i} + \sum_{i=1}^k c_i \frac{\partial}{\partial z_i}$, with $l = \dim Y$, $k = \dim Z$, $a, b_i, c_i \in C^\infty$.

nodes.name: Local form of fibred cusp differential operator
nodes.statement: $P = \sum_{|\alpha|+|\beta|+q\le m} p_{\alpha,\beta,q} (x^2 \frac{\partial}{\partial x})^q (x \frac{\partial}{\partial y})^\alpha (\frac{\partial}{\partial z})^\beta$.

nodes.name: Indicial family formula
nodes.statement: $\widehat{N_\Phi(P)}(y, \eta, \tau) = \int e^{i\eta\cdot Y} e^{i\tau S} P(0, y, z, S, Y, z-z')\, dS\, dY$.

nodes.name: Residue trace via indicial family
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{Tr}_R(A) = \frac{1}{(2\pi)^{l+1}} \int_{{}^\Phi N^* Y} \mathrm{Tr}_{\Phi^{-1}(y)}\bigl(\widehat A_{l+1}(y, \tau, \eta)\bigr)\, dy\, d\eta\, d\tau$.

nodes.name: K-theory periodicity identification
nodes.statement: $[{}^\Phi N^* Y; GL(\infty,\mathbb{C})] \cong \widetilde K^0(S^1\wedge S^1\wedge Y^{T^*Y}) \cong \widetilde K^{-2}(Y^{T^*Y}) \cong \widetilde K^0(Y^{T^*Y}) = K_c^0(T^*Y)$.

nodes.name: Standing assumption: dim Z > 0 in Section 7
nodes.statement: From section 7 onward (apart from the stabilization paragraph), $\dim Z > 0$, i.e. the typical fibre $Z$ of $\Phi: \partial X \to Y$ is at least one-dimensional.

nodes.name: Standing assumption: collar trivialization of E near boundary
nodes.statement: In a collar $\partial X \times [0,1)_x \subset X$ parametrized by the defining function $x$, $E = \pi^* E_{\partial X}$ for some $E_{\partial X} \to \partial X$, fixing a trivialization of $E$ near $\partial X$ compatible with $x$.
